sentence: The pan had no ground. This is the ground, so the devils and the scud have something to cross.

ground.note: The base material, not a decal. Replaces the untextured pan plane, so it costs no new draw call - it is a map on geometry that is already drawn.

runtime.note: Pass 02 principle 4: this is a ground plane read from 2 m to 900 m. NearestFilter with no mips aliases into sparkle the moment the craft moves, which is era-accurate degradation rather than era-accurate atmosphere. The crust is authored on the pixel grid and then filtered like any modern ground texture.

runtime.sharesMeshWith: BP_SET_DRESSING - same texture and material, so the two payloads merge into ONE mesh and ONE draw call

generation.note: Generated, not hand-placed, from one seeded stream so the layout is reproducible and reviewable. Rules are stated here rather than implied by 300 rows.
rules: 186 crack overlays at ~16 m spacing, rotated in 90-degree steps, alternating the four plate densities so no two neighbours share a scale.
Brine sheen and stain follow the three authored HZ_SALT_DRIFT spans at their own lateralFromFraction, giving each hazard's telegraph string something to be.
26 standing-brine patches beyond 24 m lateral - off the deck and off the 5.8 m open-pan run-off.
Route language twice only: a cyan edge line on both Brine Cut berms, one orange shoulder chevron run before the harvester chicane.

deckSafety.note: Every entry is surface, zero height, and therefore painted road under FLAT_FURNITURE_MAX_HEIGHT_METRES. Nothing here is furniture and nothing here has an extent above the deck. The on-deck entries are the salt-drift telegraphs, which are supposed to be on the deck - they mark a hazard the route already authored.
